Exercise 10 · Example. "I talk show in the Levant: between debate and show. Political and social talk shows occupy a prominent place in the Arab Levant television, and some reach high ratings far beyond the borders of the country from which they are broadcast. Their success is due, according to some critics, to the ability to tell people's everyday concerns in a language close to her: most guests speak in dialect, or in a mixture of dialect and dialect. fuṣḥā. These programmes, however, are being criticized more and more. Some journalists believe that several of them have turned into a "scream ring," in which guests interrupt each other and the conductors seek confrontation rather than information. "The spectator remembers the quarrel and forgets the numbers," observes a professor of Communication Sciences. The leaders, on the other hand, defend their style, claiming that the heated discussion "is part of democratic life" and that the task of those who lead is to "manage disagreement, not eliminate it." The host of a company program explains to give its guests a simple rule: "Say your opinion, then listen to that of others."
